If you opt for a more expensive treatment, the GEHA plan will cover only the amount corresponding to the least costly covered service. You'll be responsible for any additional costs, including coinsurance, that exceed this alternate benefit [p. 16][p. 27].

results.question: My dentist says they'll waive my coinsurance. Is that OK?

answer.text:
The document does not provide a specific answer regarding whether it is okay for your dentist to waive your coinsurance. You remain responsible for your coinsurance with non-PPO providers unless there is an agreement that is not specified in the evidence [p. 18].

results.question: Why do I owe more when I see an out-of-network dentist?

answer.text:
You owe more when seeing an out-of-network dentist because you pay your coinsurance plus any difference between the dentist's charges and your plan's maximum allowance. For instance, if a non-PPO dentist charges $120 and your plan's allowance is $100, you owe your coinsurance on the allowance plus the $20 difference, totaling $40 in this example [p. 18].

Additional retrieved source pages: [p. 15], [p. 28]

results.question: Are emergency dental visits covered differently?

answer.text:
Yes, emergency dental visits are covered the same as any other benefit under the GEHA dental plan [p. 18].

results.question: What if there are no in-network dentists near me?

answer.text:
If there are no in-network dentists near you, you can use out-of-network providers. The Standard Option allows for up to $2,000 in benefits for out-of-network services annually, but a $75 deductible applies. Expect higher coinsurance rates for out-of-network services [p. 18][p. 23][p. 17].

results.question: Can seasonal federal employees enroll?

answer.text:
Yes, seasonal federal employees can enroll in the FEDVIP if they are expected to work 130 hours per calendar month for at least 90 days [p. 7].

results.question: Until what age can my children stay on the plan?

answer.text:
Your children can stay on the plan until they turn 22 years old. Under specific conditions, a disabled child older than 22 may also continue coverage if they are incapable of self-support [p. 8].

results.question: Can my ex-spouse enroll in FEDVIP dental?

answer.text:

results.question: I'm retiring on MRA+10 and postponing my annuity. Does my dental continue?

results.question: Should I get an implant or a bridge for my missing molar?

answer.text:
You have the option to choose either an implant or a bridge for your missing molar. The policy covers both options, with implants having a payment limit of $2,500 (or $2,000 for Standard Option) for the calendar year [p. 32]. However, both procedures have restrictions based on the previous dental work performed on the same tooth, specifically requiring that any previous prosthesis must be unsalvageable and is subject to a 5-year replacement rule [p. 27]. Consult your dentist to evaluate which option is suitable for your situation.
